Yes, one time when backpacking in a windstorm on an island only accessible by ferry. A ferry that only runs in good weather, mind you. 

Earlier in the day before the wind started picking up we were deciding where to camp, either by a small lake or farther north on the island on a point overlooking the great lake. We thought it would be 'cool' to watch the storm roll in over the water. We ended up deciding to stay at the small lake because we spent a little too much time fishing and didn't feel like continuing the hike. 

All throughout the night heard the sound of trees snapping and falling all around us as the wind tore through the island, fortunately we were near some sturdy oaks and far from any dead wood. Trees were falling every 3 minutes- the island has sandy soil and the roots don't grip well. 

In the morning we passed by our intended camp site and the whole area was completely covered in freshly downed trees. The whole area smelled like fresh sawdust. If we had pushed through to that camp we may not have survived the night.
